item.title: Liam Coen: Brian Thomas will be able to help us make plays this week
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas didn't have any catches in the team's final two games before their Week 7 bye and he found himself on the bench for all of the second half of their Week 6 loss to the Texans, which led head coach Liam Coen to say that "guys have to step up and make plays" if they want to be on the field.
item.content:encoded:
Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas didn't have any catches in the team's final two games before their Week 7 bye and he found himself on the bench for all of the second half of their Week 6 loss to the Texans, which led head coach Liam Coen to say that "guys have to step up and make plays" if they want to be on the field.

On Monday, Coen was asked in a conference call if Thomas is going to remain out of the plans against the Colts in Jacksonville's Week 8 home game. Coen said that Thomas will have a chance to make an impact on offense.

"He's gonna be able to help us make plays this week," Coen said. "I bet it, I know it. We’re gonna continue to support him, throw our arm around him and continue to do what we gotta do to make plays on Sunday. We gotta continue to put him in the best position to do so. BT works at it. He cares about this, he cares about winning and losing, he cares about his team. We all wanna see guys have success individually, but I'm excited about attacking this week with BT."

With a couple of weeks to go before the trade deadline and the Jaguars employing a deep group of receivers, there will likely continue to be chatter about Thomas being on the move before November 10 whether he makes it back onto the stat sheet or not this week.

item.title: Mike Macdonald: It'd be crazy not to make Jaxon Smith-Njigba the primary target as much as you can
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Seattle's HC noted that Smith-Njigba's remarkable start to the 2026 season is largely by design.
item.content:encoded:
Jaxon Smith-Njigba continued his remarkable start to the 2026 season on Sunday with nine catches for 150 yards and a touchdown against the Chiefs.

He also had a pair of carries to give him 163 yards from scrimmage.

If it seems like the Seahawks are giving him an inordinate amount of targets, it’s because they are.

Wouldn’t you?

“You'd be crazy not to try to make him the primary [target] on as many concepts as you can,” head coach Mike Macdonald said in his postgame press conference after Sunday’s win.

Through seven games, Smith-Njigba leads the league in receiving yards (867) and receiving touchdowns (eight). He also leads the league in targets (78).

“He's tremendous,” Macdonald said. “I don't know how else to describe him. Like, he's had some adversity this week. Just going to leave it like that. Just really proud of him as a person. He's a person, competitor, teammate. How do you not just have the most respect for the guy and love him for how he operates?”

If there was any play emblematic of Smith-Njigba’s ability and skill as a receiver, it was his 28-yard touchdown catch late in the second quarter to put the Seahawks up 10-0. With Smith-Njigba matched up one-on-one with a Chiefs cornerback, there was little doubt as to where the ball would go once the ball was snapped to quarterback Sam Darnold.

“I have pretty good confidence that if we're throwing him the ball, he's going to come down with it,” Macdonald said. "When you see him singled like that, based off that play call, I knew that's where Sam was going to go with the ball.”

Smith-Njigba has eclipsed 100 yards in six of his seven games this season, reaching 120 in five of them. If he continues like this, the reigning AP offensive player of the year could be in line to get some MVP votes at season’s end.

item.title: Tom Brady's criticism of officials tests limits of what a team owner can say
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Brady is prohibited from "egregious" criticism of calls.
item.content:encoded:
Tom Brady's insistence on working for Fox while owning a piece of the Raiders creates potential complications beyond the restrictions on his access to team facilities and practices. When it comes to criticizing game officials, there's a line he can't cross.

As the league has previously explained it, Brady is prohibited from being "egregiously critical of officiating" or "call[ing] into question the integrity of an official or the crew."

On Sunday in Detroit, Brady criticized multiple officiating decisions. The overriding question is whether the league office will regard the criticism as "egregious."

In the third quarter, Packers linebacker Brenton Cox Jr. knocked Lions quarterback Jared Goff to the ground after a throw. The officials called Cox for roughing the passer.

"Not much at all," Brady said over the replay. "It's coming off the block. His face is buried. I don't know about that. I mean . . . that's a tough one."

Fox rules analyst (and former NFL senior V.P. of officiating) Dean Blandino agreed. "He's coming off the block," Blandino said. "You really want to see more force there. It's almost like he's just trying to keep himself up. There's no real extension. I don't like that as roughing."

"I don't like it either," Brady said.

In the fourth quarter, after Lions linebacker Derrick Barnes was flagged for an illegal hit on Packers running back MarShawn Lloyd, Brady was blunt.

"What?" Brady said. "There's no way. . . . Oh, come on, man. Come on. [Jordan] Love throws it over the middle. There's linebackers in the middle. He's just turning his right shoulder away from it. That's allowed 99 out of 100 [times]. . . . It's a bang-bang play. I know in super slow-mo every little minute frame looks like a lot, but when you're on the field, you've got to pursue that ball. If [Lloyd] catches it, [Barnes] needs force to knock him on the ground. He needs force to knock that ball out. . . . He can't go in there and put his hand on him."

Later, during Detroit's game-winning drive, Brady sounded off on a questionable roughing the passer call, after Packers defensive tackle Karl Brooks hit Lions quarterback Jared Goff following a throw.

"Oh my goodness, what is that?" Brady said. "There's no way! Brooks on the tackle. Kind of makes a great play. It's a bang-bang play. He rolls off his body. It's a great throw by Goff. It's definitely not roughing the passer. I mean, you just — you're just ripping through the line of scrimmage to try to get the quarterback on the ground. Look, I love Goff standing there in the pocket. But you just can't keep tacking on 15 yards."

Blandino agreed with Brady's assessment again. "It wasn't late," Blandino said. "They might have said head/neck area. But this is not head/neck area. His head is up. That's teach-tape tackle. That's not roughing the passer."

Each of the calls seemed unwarranted. But the league's rules don't create an exception based on accuracy of the criticism. Team personnel (including owners) can only say so much when it comes to publicly criticizing officials.

Is it "egregious"? The folks at Merriam-Webster define the term as "very noticeable." If that's the same definition the NFL uses, Brady's comments qualify.

It has nothing to do with Brady's role as a broadcaster. (If anything, Kevin Burkhardt's criticism of the calls was even stronger.) However, the league has a policy that muzzles team personnel, including owners.

If Brady gets dinged for this, it's not because he's working for Fox. It's because he's working for Fox while owning a piece of the Raiders.

item.title: Ravens' second-half meltdown was unlike any choke the NFL has seen in more than 75 years
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Ravens had a choke of epic proportions on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
The Ravens had a choke of epic proportions on Sunday.

Winning 13-0 at halftime, Baltimore ended up losing to Cincinnati, 35-13. The Bengals' win was the first time since 1950 that an NFL team has won a game by 20 or more points after trailing by 13 or more points at halftime.

It's hard to describe just how much the Bengals dominated the second half. The first 10 possessions of the second half went like this: Bengals touchdown, Ravens punt, Bengals touchdown, Ravens turnover on downs, Bengals touchdown, Ravens punt, Bengals touchdown, Ravens interception, Bengals touchdown, Ravens turnover on downs.

The Ravens' loss was their second consecutive ugly second half: A week earlier, Baltimore was beating Cleveland 10-0 at halftime but ended up losing 13-10. Over the last two weeks, the Ravens have been outscored 48-0 in the second half.

Whatever the Ravens are doing at halftime, it's not working, and it needs to get fixed ahead of this Sunday's game at Buffalo.

item.title: Report: Aaron Jones considered day-to-day with knee injury
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: There is some positive news on the injury front for the undefeated Vikings.
item.content:encoded:
There is some positive news on the injury front for the undefeated Vikings.

While running back Aaron Jones had to depart Sunday's win over the Colts with a knee injury, it is not considered to be significant at this time, ESPN's Adam Schefter reports.

Jones was described as day-to-day.

Jones has been dealing with injury issues throughout 2026, but has not yet missed a game. He has rushed for 436 yards with two touchdowns and caught 13 passes for 72 yards.

Jones departed Sunday’s game having rushed for 26 yards on eight carries. Jordan Mason had the bulk of the work at running back, rushing for 68 yards on 15 attempts.

The 6-0 Vikings will be on the road to face the 4-2 Lions on Sunday afternoon in Week 8.

item.title: Patriots releasing P Bryce Baringer off injured reserve
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: If a team needs a punter, a new one is hitting the market.
item.content:encoded:
If a team needs a punter, a new one is hitting the market.

New England is releasing Bryce Baringer, according to Jordan Schultz of The Schultz Report.

Baringer has a sixth-round pick in 2023, had served as New England’s punter for the last three seasons. In averaged 47.4 yards per punt in 2025 with a 40.6-yard net average.

He has been on injured reserve, with veteran Mitch Wishnowsky handling New England’s punt duties so far this season.

After Thursday's loss to the Bears, the Patriots will be on the road to face the Dolphins in Week 8.

item.title: With games against the Bills and Jaguars looming, the Ravens need Lamar Jackson
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: There's no uncertainty as to whether the Ravens need quarterback Lamar Jackson.
item.content:encoded:
There's no uncertainty as to whether the Ravens need quarterback Lamar Jackson. There's plenty of uncertainty as to when he'll be able to play.

With him, they're 3-1. Without him, they're 1-2. With losses to the Browns and Bengals in the past eight days, the Ravens have started 0-2 in the AFC North for the first time since 2007.

Jackson made it clear on Friday that he's dealing with a high-ankle sprain, suffered in Week 4 against the Titans. He said at the time, as to the possibility of playing on Sunday against Cincinnati, “Right now, I’m heading in the right direction."

One day later, the Ravens downgraded Jackson from questionable to out.

With a Sunday trip to Buffalo coming, followed by a short-week visit from the Jaguars, Jackson's return becomes critical. Absent Jackson, Baltimore's 4-3 record could sink to 4-5 by next Friday.

So the question of the week in Baltimore becomes whether Jackson will play against Josh Allen and the Bills. As mentioned on Sunday's Football Night in America, it's unknown within the building whether he'll be able to return on Sunday — and any effort to predict when he'll be able to play is a guess.

Jackson made it clear during his Friday press conference that it's an issue of pain tolerance, and that the ankle sprain is keeping him from being as mobile as he needs to be. That's no surprise. A high-ankle sprain takes more time to heal than other types of sprains. He explained that he doesn't want to play if doing so would potentially hurt the team.

The challenge this week for the Ravens will be to get the eventual starter ready for the game. If Jackson is listed as a "full" participant on Wednesday, Thursday, and/or Friday, it will mean he has taken 100 percent of his normal first-team reps. Which also will mean that, if he doesn't play, backup Tyler Huntley won't be getting the first-team reps in preparation for Buffalo.

With or without Jackson, the next two games become critical to Baltimore's season. Win both, and they're right on track for reaching their goal. Lose both, and it could be another season without a ticket to the postseason party.

The chances of going 2-0, and not 0-2, will be much greater if Jackson is able to play. It's something that we'll find out as the current week unfolds.

item.title: Zaire Franklin dealing with hairline fracture, Sean Rhyan believed to have high-ankle sprain
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Packers have a couple of impact players who are dealing with injuries.
item.content:encoded:
The Packers have a couple of impact players who are dealing with injuries.

According to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, linebacker Zaire Franklin is dealing with a hairline fracture in his leg, while center Sean Rhyan is believed to have suffered a high-ankle sprain.

Franklin's injury occurred in practice last week. He missed Sunday's game against the Lions but is expected to return without missing much more time. The team did not place him on injured reserve, which is another indication of his status.

Rhyan went down during the first half of Sunday's loss to Detroit. If his high-ankle sprain diagnosis is confirmed, he's likely to be out for four-to-six weeks.

Green Bay has a short week coming up, as they will host the Panthers on Thursday night.

item.title: Kevin O'Connell: We're confident we're not far off offensively
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: With the 49ers and Chiefs losing on Sunday, the Vikings are the last unbeaten team standing in the NFL and they are in some rare company when it comes to how they're winning games.
item.content:encoded:
With the 49ers and Chiefs losing on Sunday, the Vikings are the last unbeaten team standing in the NFL and they are in some rare company when it comes to how they're winning games.

The Vikings have scored 10 touchdowns in their six wins and, per ESPN, they are tied for the third-fewest touchdowns during a 6-0 start in NFL history. On Sunday, the team scored its only touchdown to take their first lead of the day in the fourth quarter and they finished their 16-10 win over the Colts with 275 yards of offense.

After the game, head coach Kevin O'Connell pointed out near misses in the passing game and penalties as things that kept the offense from finding a groove and said that there's strong belief that things are going to fall into place.

"I think our guys are very confident that we're not far off," O'Connell said. "The far off changes a little bit as you go, but I'm very, very confident we'll get it going."

The Vikings will kick off November with a trip to Detroit before moving on to face the Bills, Packers, 49ers and Falcons over the rest of the month. That makes it an ideal time for them to make a move from "not far off" to clicking in a way that will allow them to remain at the front of the NFC playoff race.

item.title: Report: NFL "furious" over Eagles' handling of the Jalen Hurts messaging
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The NFL reportedly has no issue with the manner in which the Eagles handled the health of quarterback Jalen Hurts in London.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL reportedly has no issue with the manner in which the Eagles handled the health of quarterback Jalen Hurts in London. In contrast, the league is not thrilled with the manner in which the team handled the ensuing controversy.

Marcus Hayes of the Philadelphia Inquirer, citing an unnamed "longtime source well-connected to the NFL offices," reports that the powers-that-be are "furious" with the team for its messaging regarding the situation.

To date, only coach Nick Sirianni has been made available to answer the obvious follow-up questions raised by a pair of statements issued by the team. Sirianni didn't have much to say, regardless of whether he did (or didn't) know more about the matter than he shared.

G.M. Howie Roseman, who runs the entire football operation, has not addressed the issue. The doctors who evaluated Hurts have not been made available.

Through it all, the team has hidden behind "patient privacy" — even after the statements shared specific details about the "superficial" blood clot that became a deep vein thrombosis and multiple blood clots in his lungs. The medical privacy rights of Jalen Hurts have already been compromised, if not expressly waived. Specific questions about how the initial condition arose, when it was diagnosed, how it was treated, and whether the complications flowed from those decisions are irrelevant at this point to the issue of privacy.

Of course, the NFL didn't help the situation via the dismissive comments made by multiple executives last week, including chief medical officer Allen Sills. His insistence that Hurts had "very conservative" care doesn't mesh on the surface with the decision to let him fly to London, to play in London, and to fly home from London.

On Sunday, the NFL and NFL Players Association jointly announced that they are "working together" on the Hurts case. It's unclear what that means, especially since the NFLPA has not yet officially invoked its unilateral right to demand an investigation under Article 39, Section 5(f) of the Collective Bargaining Agreement.

The union can't afford the perception of complicity in a possible coverup. Any investigation, in whatever form it takes, must seek real answers to hard questions and provide them to the public.

It's impossible for the NFL to, on one hand, welcome public attention, engagement, and stadium funding while, on the other, say "none of your damn business" when the public has natural curiosity about the things that happen to NFL players. Last week, the Eagles failed to satisfy the widespread interest in Hurts's case. Moving forward, any effort to investigate what happened must include a commitment to true and complete transparency.

Through it all, the Eagles play a home game tonight against the Cowboys. It will be interesting to see whether and to what extent ESPN's wall-to-wall coverage of the game advances the lingering Hurts story.

item.title: John Harbaugh: Sunday was a pivotal game, our guys took the bull by the horns
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Giants came into Sunday's game in Houston off a tie and a loss that led to a quarterback change and oddsmakers installed them as heavy underdogs as a result.
item.content:encoded:
The Giants came into Sunday's game in Houston off a tie and a loss that led to a quarterback change and oddsmakers installed them as heavy underdogs as a result.

That proved to be a miscalculation. The Giants led for much of the first half and moved back in front in the fourth quarter before the Texans were able to rally and send the game to overtime. The Giants defense forced a stop and two big runs by Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary gave them a walk-off 27-21 win in their final game before the bye.

Skattebo, Singletary, and Tyrone Tracy combined to run 28 times for 180 yards while J.J. McCarthy went 20-of-28 for 252 yards as part of a full-team effort that earned praise from head coach John Harbaugh after the game. Harbaugh said that people were "going to find out about who they are" in this game and that the players "took the bull by the horns" to improve to 4-2-1.

"The two most important games of the season will be coming up after we come back from the bye, which will set the direction for the rest of the season really," Harbaugh said, via a transcript from the team. "But we're going to be in this thing until the end now. This was a pivotal game. This was a really high-pressure game for our team. We didn't talk about that, but they all knew how important this game was, and they responded accordingly."

Regardless of what happens on Monday night or next week, the Giants know they'll be in first place when they return to the field against the Eagles in Week 9. They'll follow that with a quick turnaround to the Commanders on Thursday night, which gives them a chance to take the NFC East by the horns at the start of the second half. Sunday's performance provided plenty of reason to think they can do exactly that.

item.title: Falcons rookie Kendal Daniels goes from hospital to hero in a week
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Falcons rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels left the field on a stretcher last Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
Falcons rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels left the field on a stretcher last Sunday. A week later, he left the field a hero of the Falcons' 29-20 upset of the previously undefeated 49ers.

"It's been the craziest week of my life," Daniels said, via Marc Raimondi of ESPN. "I've never not walked off the field after an injury. So, mentally, I had to be prepared and going back home and just making sure I was OK mentally more than anything and not playing timid, but I've never not gotten up from an injury. So, being stretched off the field -- I won't let it happen again. It was a bad feeling, and I'm blessed to be able to play this week."

Last week, Daniels dove to tackle Bears tight end Colston Loveland in the third quarter and Daniels' head collided with Loveland's left leg. Medical personnel attended to Daniels for almost 8 minutes before sending him to a local hospital for further evaluation of his neck.

On Sunday, Daniels iced the game with an interception of Brock Purdy. He also had nine solo tackles and a fumble recovery.

Coach Kevin Stefanski called it "remarkable."

"I wasn't thinking of [his neck injury]," Daniels said. "'I think that was the last thing I was worried about was last week."

item.title: Aaron Glenn defends not using timeouts after saying he should have on Sunday
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said after Sunday's 28-25 loss to the Dolphins that he should have used the team's timeouts at the end of the first half rather than letting the Dolphins drain the clock before scoring a touchdown to go up 14 points with six seconds left on the clock.
item.content:encoded:
Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said after Sunday's 28-25 loss to the Dolphins that he should have used the team's timeouts at the end of the first half rather than letting the Dolphins drain the clock before scoring a touchdown to go up 14 points with six seconds left on the clock.

The Dolphins picked up a first down at the Jets' 25-yard-line on the first play after the two-minute warning and then picked up 20 yards on their next two plays. They took their own timeout with 20 seconds left, drew a pass interference penalty in the end zone and used a second timeout after losing yards on a run before scoring on a Malik Willis run.

On Monday, Glenn defended the team's approach despite his Sunday admission that he should have stopped the clock.

"They have time to get more first downs to negate the timeouts that we have, so we call timeout then we’re using those," Glenn said. "They get another first down, then they can run the clock out."

The Jets had more to gain from getting the ball back with time to mount a drive than they had to lose by using their timeouts in that situation and the mismanagement highlights a consistent problem of Glenn's tenure with the team. The Jets have now been outscored 107-6 in the last two minutes of the first halves since Glenn was hired and the head coach said Monday that they are "trying" to improve in those situations.

Based on Sunday, one approach might be to do the opposite of whatever first comes to mind on the sideline.

item.title: Baker Mayfield: Sunday's win was a statement of our potential
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield said his right thumb might be a little sore after Sunday's win over the Panthers moved the team to 2-5, but he did it with a smile because the cause of the soreness was how often he handed the ball off.
item.content:encoded:
Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield said his right thumb might be a little sore after Sunday's win over the Panthers moved the team to 2-5, but he did it with a smile because the cause of the soreness was how often he handed the ball off.

The Bucs ran all over the Panthers en route to a 43-13 win, which meant Mayfield only had to throw the ball 11 times in his return from missing three games with a dislocated thumb. Bucky Irving, Kenneth Gainwell, and Sean Tucker ran 45 times for 246 yards in the victory and Mayfield said after it was over that the Bucs need to take it as proof of what they're capable of doing.

"I think it's a statement internally for us, not to anybody else, but for us," Mayfield said, via the team's website. "This is what it's supposed to look like. No, it's not always going to look like that, it's the NFL, but operation-wise and when it comes to complementary football, this is what the potential for this team can have so it's a statement within ourselves."

The Bucs' 1-5 start made it hard to see much positive about how things will play out, but Sunday's game was their first in the NFC South and no one has come close to running away with the division. Posting another win against the Falcons next Sunday would make their position look even better and Sunday's performance provided reason for confidence that they can pull that off.

item.title: Klint Kubiak on QB change: We're thinking about everything to fix our problems
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Raiders lost their fourth straight game on Sunday and head coach Klint Kubiak said that nothing is off the table as they consider ways to halt their slide.
item.content:encoded:
The Raiders lost their fourth straight game on Sunday and head coach Klint Kubiak said that nothing is off the table as they consider ways to halt their slide.

That includes a quarterback change. Kirk Cousins's play may not be at the top of the list of issues hampering the team, but first overall pick Fernando Mendoza is going to be the starter at some point and Kubiak was asked after Sunday's 35-21 loss to the Rams if it is time to start thinking about that future when it comes to who is piloting the offense.

“I think we have to go watch the film," Kubiak said. "I think at this point, we're thinking about everything to fix our problems, how to fix our issues in the red zone, in the third quarter, personnel, scheme. We've got to talk about all of it."

Part of the consideration for the Raiders is how well they can support Mendoza at this point in the season. The team's running game is offering little support and they've given up at least 30 points in each of their four losses, which is a combination that does no favors to any quarterback.

The schedule brings a bit of a reprieve next week with the Jets, but the 49ers, Seahawks and Broncos are on deck after that. It's hard to see the Raiders coming out of that stretch in playoff contention if those problems remain in place and that might make it time to turn things over to the rookie.

item.title: Dolphins, Jets bring plenty of futility into their first meeting of the year
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Dolphins emerge from their bye without a win and, amazingly, without holding the lead at any point in their five losses.
item.content:encoded:
The Dolphins emerge from their bye without a win and, amazingly, without holding the lead at any point in their five losses. They get a chance to change both trends by facing a division rival against whom they've had plenty of recent success.

The Dolphins are 2-9 on the road since the start of the 2025 season. One of those wins came at MetLife Stadium against the Jets, where the Dolphins play today. Elsewhere, they're 1-9.

The Jets, in turn, are 0-7 in the AFC East under coach Aaron Glenn, and 0-1 this season.

A loss by the Dolphins would drop them to 0-6 for the first time since 2019, the notorious tank season that allegedly included owner Stephen Ross offering former head coach Brian Flores $100,000 per loss. (They went 5-5 over the final 10 games that year.)

However this one goes, watch the final two minutes of the first half. Under Glenn, the Jets have been outscored 100-6 in the last 120 seconds before intermission. If that continues, it's another reason for Glenn to potentially be heading for a permanent intermission.

item.title: Jonathan Taylor: Trade rumors are out there, my wife discussing it doesn't change anything
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Colts' decision to fire General Manager Chris Ballard last week has led to speculation about what other moves are coming for the team and particular attention has been paid to potential trades.
item.content:encoded:
The Colts' decision to fire General Manager Chris Ballard last week has led to speculation about what other moves are coming for the team and particular attention has been paid to potential trades.

Running back Jonathan Taylor's name has come up in that speculation and he said last week that he hasn't given any thought to a move because his focus is on playing. Taylor's wife Ayanna doesn't have games to prepare for, however, and she made a couple of social media videos discussing the possibility of a trade over the weekend.

Those videos laid out the case for why the Colts would trade Taylor, including the lack of a 2027 first-round pick due to Ballard's trade for Sauce Gardner. After Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Vikings, Taylor was asked about those videos and he said he doesn't think his wife is only talking about things that already in the larger conversations surrounding the team.

“I think it’s been out there already, so I think her adding [to it] doesn’t really change anything,” Taylor said, via James Boyd of TheAthletic.com. “You know everybody’s on TikTok these days. So, you just have to come into work and stay focused.”

Taylor's teammates Quenton Nelson and DeForest Bucker have also seen their names come up in trade chatter and the only way that's likely to stop before November 10 is if the Colts is if they go ahead with moves involving all three players.

item.title: NFL kickers are 167-for-170 from inside 37 yards. Trey Smack had 2 of the 3 misses Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Once an NFL offense gets inside the 20-yard line, coming away with at least a field goal should be just about a sure thing.
item.content:encoded:
Once an NFL offense gets inside the 20-yard line, coming away with at least a field goal should be just about a sure thing. It wasn't for the Packers on Sunday in Detroit.

Packers kicker Trey Smack missed a 26-yard field goal wide right, and had a 35-yard field goal blocked, in the Packers' 20-17 loss to the Lions.

How rare is it for an NFL kicker to miss field goals that short? So far this season, NFL kickers are 167-for-170 on field goals from inside 37 yards. Smack had two of the three misses on Sunday, and the other was a 23-yarder by Bears kicker Cairo Santos that was blocked by the Vikings in Week 2.

The last time a kicker missed two field goals of 35 yards or shorter in the same game was seven years ago, when Patriots kicker Mike Nugent missed two in a game against the Browns. Nugent was cut afterward.

Packers coach Matt LaFleur says Smack won’t get cut. At least not yet. But it's safe to say Smack's seat is getting hot.

item.title: Sunday Night Football: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Seahawks defense dominate Chiefs, win 20-3
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Smith-Njigba had 150 yards while Seattle's defense stifled QB Patrick Mahomes and Kansas City's offense all night.
item.content:encoded:
The defending Super Bowl champions looked like they could ride their defense to another title on Sunday night.

Seattle's defense and receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba were the stars on Sunday night, as the Seahawks defeated the Chiefs 20-3.

Kansas City was held off-balance throughout the night, leading to one of the lowest-scoring outputs of the Mahomes era. The Seahawks held the Chiefs to just 11 first downs, 213 yards, and 3-11 on third down.

While no one had contained Kenneth Walker all year, the Seahawks were able to slow down their former running back. Walker rushed 14 times for 36 yards, averaging a paltry 2.6 yards per carry. He entered Sunday’s game averaging 6.3 over Kansas City’s first five contests.

Mahomes finished the game 19-of-33 for 165 yards with an interception, working out to a 58.3 passer rating. Mahomes has finished with a worse passer rating in just four other regular-season starts in his career.

As noted by the NBC broadcast, this was the first time the Chiefs did not even reach the red zone in a Mahomes start — including the postseason.

Tight end Travis Kelce led with four receptions for 44 yards. He moved into fifth place all-time in receptions, but that’s likely little consolation given the result.

On the other side, Sam Darnold finished 20-of-28 for 257 yards with a touchdown and an interception. That pick nearly led to Chiefs points at the end of the first half, but Harrison Butker’s 58-yard field goal attempt fell short.

That was one of two misses from Butker, who also sent a 45-yard attempt wide right midway through the fourth quarter. That would have put the Chiefs down by seven with 8:33 to go.

After the miss, Seattle put the game away with Emanuel Wilson’s 21-yard touchdown run.

The Seahawks finished with 24 first downs, 410 total yards, and 11-of-16 on third down.

Smith-Njigba set the pace, catching nine passes for 150 yards with a touchdown. The reigning AP offensive player of the year has registered at least 100 yards in six of his seven games so far this season, with five performances of at least 120 yards.

The game’s result leaves the Vikings as the lone unbeaten team entering Week 8, as the 49ers also lost to the Falcons earlier on Sunday.

Back above .500, the 4-3 Seahawks will host the 5-2 Bears next Monday night.

Now at 5-1, the Chiefs will be back on the road next week to face the 5-2 Broncos on Sunday afternoon.

item.title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba on pace to break Calvin Johnson's yardage record, with a game to spare
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: After his huge performance on Sunday night, the Seahawks' star receiver has 867 yards through seven games.
item.content:encoded:
Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba is on pace to break Calvin Johnson's NFL record for receiving yards in a season. And Smith-Njigba is on pace to do it without even needing the 17th game of the season.

Through seven games this season, Smith-Njigba has 867 receiving yards. That's a pace of 123.9 yards per game.

When Johnson set a new NFL record with 1,964 receiving yards in 2012, it was a 16-game season, so Johnson averaged 122.8 yards per game.

So if Smith-Njigba keeps at his current pace, he'll break Johnson's record in the 16th game of the season, when he would be at 1,982 games. Smith-Njigba could break Johnson's record without even needing the benefit of the 17-game season.

Smith-Njigba's 17-game pace is 2,106 yards, which would give him the only 2,000-yard receiving season in NFL history.

Last season Smith-Njigba was the NFL's Offensive Player of the Year, but this season he's been even better. He's on his way to what might be the best season any wide receiver has ever had.

item.title: Packers S Xavier McKinney: I see what's going on with officiating and it's killing us
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur got heated with officials several times during Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Lions, but he didn't want to make them the focus of his postgame comments.
item.content:encoded:
Packers head coach Matt LaFleur got heated with officials several times during Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Lions, but he didn't want to make them the focus of his postgame comments.

LaFleur said there were "some tough calls," but that his team needed to rise above them. Among those tough calls were two roughing the passer penalties and an unnecessary roughness call on defensive tackle Devonte Wyatt for a hit that came without a clear whistle to stop play as Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown got up to continue running.

While LaFleur didn't want to unload on the officials, safety Xavier McKinney was more willing to go there. He said it is not "great officiating" and that the calls are "kind of f—-ing up" the team's games. McKinney knows that could earn him a monetary penalty from the league, but he said he's fine with that because he feels he's telling the truth.

"I would rather get fined and try to help my team out because I see what's going on, and it's killing us," McKinney said, via Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com. "We all see it. We all see what's going on. Everyone sees what's going on, the fans see what's going on, we see what's going on when we're out there."

All of the calls can't explain everything about the loss — Packers rookie Trey Smack missed a 26-yard field goal and had a 35-yarder blocked at the end of drives that could have also been finished with touchdowns — but McKinney's comments make it clear that they played a role.

item.title: Christian McCaffrey not worried about thigh injury moving forward
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The 49ers have dealt with a slew of injuries this season, so they were likely bracing for the worst when running back Christian McCaffrey was forced out of Sunday's game against the Falcons with a thigh injury in the first quarter.
item.content:encoded:
The 49ers have dealt with a slew of injuries this season, so they were likely bracing for the worst when running back Christian McCaffrey was forced out of Sunday's game against the Falcons with a thigh injury in the first quarter.

McCaffrey was able to return in the second half, but his presence wasn't enough to stop the team from suffering their first loss of the 2026 season. After the game, McCaffrey said that he felt like his leg "just died on me" and that he was frustrated trying to get back on track the rest of the day before adding that he doesn't expect the issue to linger into the future.

"I'll be fine. I'm not worried about it," McCaffrey said, via 49ersWebzone.com. "It just sucks to me because that was one of those ones where I just felt like I could have got going . . . I was just trying to keep it warm and not make it worse, but there's only so much you can do to get back to where you want to be. I'll be fine. I know that. I'll be all right."

The 49ers have a bye in Week 8 and McCaffrey won't be the only one hoping to use it as time to to get closer to full strength heading into the second half of the season.

item.title: Mike Vrabel: No concern about A.J. Brown, just have to get into rhythm
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Patriots wide receiver A.J.
item.content:encoded:
Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown's return to action the last two weeks has not resulted in the kind of production that the team was hoping to see.

Brown has been targeted with 16 passes from Drake Maye, but they've only resulted in six catches for 75 yards. His first game back featured multiple drops and the results have sparked some concern about whether Brown is struggling to fit into the offense after missing four games with an ankle injury.

That concern is not shared by head coach Mike Vrabel, however.

“No, I don’t have any concern. . . . I thought that he dropped a few passes, and then the other night there was a contested catch that — I’ve seen him make those plays in the past, I’ve seen those plays get called for DPI, and I’ve seen those plays be good plays by the defense down the field,” Vrabel said on WEEI Monday. “So, I don’t think anybody has to press here or anything else. I think we just have to get back into a rhythm offensively with the guys that we have.”

Brown's return against the Jets in Week 6 was followed by a quick turnaround to last Thursday's game against the Bears. He and the Patriots will have a full week to work on things before facing the Dolphins next Sunday.

item.title: Cam Skattebo on penalty for lowering his helmet: I'm going to keep doing it
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Giants running back Cam Skattebo got an unnecessary roughness penalty on Sunday for lowering his helmet into a Texans defender.
item.content:encoded:
Giants running back Cam Skattebo got an unnecessary roughness penalty on Sunday for lowering his helmet into a Texans defender. That penalty is rarely called on ball carriers, but Skattebo says he's going to keep doing it no matter how often they flag him.

After the game, Skattebo declined to elaborate on the conversation he had with the official who flagged him but did criticize the NFL for sometimes using hits that draw penalties or fines for promotional clips. And Skattebo insisted that he's going to keep his running style going.

"I'll keep that conversation between us, but I will say, the NFL loves to post me when I do stuff like that but then also wants to take stuff from me," Skattebo said. "I'm going to run the ball like I want to run the ball. And if I'm going to continue to get flags for it or fined for it, guess I'm going to play for free. I'm going to do everything I can to be on this team, to give everything I've got, and if they're going to punish me for that I'm just going to keep doing it, keep playing hard."

At some point, the NFL may give Skattebo no choice but to stop if he keeps getting flags and is eventually suspended. But until that point, he says fines will not be a deterrent to playing the way he wants to play.

item.title: Mike Tomlin supports Dan Campbell's late fourth-down decision
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Mike Tomlin has no qualms regarding a decision from Dan Campbell that may have seemed curious on the surface.
item.content:encoded:
Mike Tomlin has no qualms regarding a decision from Dan Campbell that may have seemed curious on the surface.

Facing fourth and one from the Detroit 24 with 4:53 to play, Campbell opted to go for it. The play resulted in a two-yard loss, and a very short field for the Packers.

“I thought we would get it, number one," Campbell said after the game. "I really believed we would get that. Number two, I knew we would get the ball back if it didn’t work out. Those were the two thoughts."

After Sunday night's Chiefs-Seahawks game, NBC's Mike Tirico asked Tomlin for his take on Campbell's decision.

"It centers around elite quarterback play," Tomlin said. "When you got elite quarterback play, and particularly when you're playing elite quarterback play, you want to make sure your guy at least has a chance to have the ball at the end of the game. And that's what that decision appeared to be about for me. If he punts that ball the way Jordan Love and company has been operating, it's not possible, it's probable that they're gonna matriculate the ball down the field and win the game.  And so what he did by going for it, he was either gonna be successful and keep the ball for his quarterback, or he was at least gonna give his quarterback an opportunity to answer. I was always ready to make that decision when I had Big Ben [Roethlisberger], for example, and I was facing another elite quarterback."

The Lions got the ball back because their defense stiffened, forcing a field goal try. And because the Detroit special-teams unit blocked the 35-yard try.

But even if the Packers had scored a touchdown, the drive started with 4:50 to play. The Lions would have had a chance to answer.

And that's only if the Lions first failed to gain a yard on fourth down by handing it to Jahmyr Gibbs.

It's another tangible example of the key differences between analytics and feel. The coach, considering all circumstances, knew it was the right call.

That said, the age of analytics had made it much easier to do something that would have once been ignored as unconventional, since reliance on the math has torn down the wall between what is and isn't "normal" for a coach to do.

And Tomlin's past actions give his words even more credence. Via NBC Sports research, Campbell was the first coach to go for it on fourth down inside his own 25 in a tie game since Week 1 of the 2014 season.

That day, Tomlin's Steelers ran a fake punt from their own 20 in a 27-27 game against the Browns. It happened with 9:48 to play in a 27-27 game. The play worked, the drive later stalled at the 50, and the Steelers won with a walk-off field goal, 30-27.

item.title: Nick Emmanwori: Seahawks' defense was motivated to stop Kenneth Walker
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Walker entered Sunday night averaging 133 rushing yards a game. The Seahawks held him to 36 yards.
item.content:encoded:
Heading into Sunday night in Seattle, the story of the game was Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker, who was off to an outstanding start to this season after leaving the Seahawks in free agency. After the game, the story was the Seahawks' defense shutting Walker down.

Seahawks safety Nick Emmanwori admitted after the game that he and his teammates were motivated to hold Walker in check, knowing how many people were criticizing the Seahawks for letting the reigning Super Bowl MVP leave for Kansas City in free agency.

"I ain't gonna lie, I did," Emmanwori said. "I'm not gonna sit here and lie. I definitely did want to hold him under 100. I don't really listen to all the media noise but that was my motivation. I know a lot of dudes on defense, that was their motivation, too, to stop him under 100 and play lights out on defense and I think we did that."

The Seahawks did more than just hold Walker under 100 yards. They held him to 36 yards on 14 carries, by far his worst game of this season and almost 100 yards below his average heading into Sunday night of 133 yards per game.

Meanwhile, the Seahawks' much-maligned rushing game had a big night, with running back Emanuel Wilson gaining 100 yards and a touchdown and the Seahawks as a team gaining 153 rushing yards — more than triple the Chiefs' total.

The Seahawks won 20-3, and the defense was disappointed because they wanted it to be 20-0.

"We put on a clinic," Emmanwori said. "I know the defense, a lot of dudes were upset that we didn't give them a zero. That was our goal, give them zero. We definitely could've accomplished that. But that just says what type of defense we are. There's a lot of talk out there about what type of defense we are, if we've still got it or whatever. But we don't really pay attention to that, and we knew what we was fitting to do. None of us, we didn't lose any sleep about any offense or who we're facing."

Who they were facing was the player who led the way as they won the Super Bowl eight months ago. But now he's in a different uniform, and the Seahawks wanted to show that they're the same Super Bowl team without him that they were with him.

item.title: Anthony Richardson doesn't regret his recent arrest for marijuana posession
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson was arrested last week for marijuana possession — presumably without taking a plutonium-powered Delorean back to 1955.
item.content:encoded:
Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson was arrested last week for marijuana possession — presumably without taking a plutonium-powered Delorean back to 1955.

The Colts, as explained by James Boyd of The Athletic, made Richardson available to speak to reporters after Sunday's loss at Minnesota.

Via Boyd, Richardson was asked whether he regrets the incident.

“I enjoy life," Richardson said. "I don’t really regret a lot of things I do. I appreciate my life. I appreciate God waking me up every morning."

Richardson also said this about the incident, per Stephen Holder of ESPN: "I know my character, God knows my character, my family knows me. So I don't need to explain anything else."

Given the widespread legalization of marijuana possession and use in 2026, Richardson has no general reason to believe that possessing or using marijuana reflects poorly on his character. More specifically, however, the arrest exposes him to discipline under the substance-abuse policy.

From Section 2.3 of the policy: "Absent aggravating circumstances, discipline for a first offense will be a suspension without pay for up to four (4) regular and/or post-season games."

It sounds ridiculous in this day and age, but Indiana has yet to join the many states that have abandoned outdated marijuana laws (except, apparently, while smoking it on the air during a TV show originating there). Now, unless Richardson avoids a conviction, a guilty plea, a no-contest plea, or a diversion program arising from the incident, Richardson will eventually be facing a four-game suspension and the significant loss of revenue coming from it.

Because, again, players who are suspended lose 100 percent of their income during the suspension — unlike owners. If Richardson's case isn't resolved until 2027 (a bench trial was set for January 4), and if he signs somewhere next year even for the league minimum based on his experience of $1.26 million, he'll lose $280,000.

Hopefully, the next CBA will be further tweaked to eliminate this provision from the substance-abuse policy. It's outdated, it's onerous, and it creates bizarre outcomes where players who have no control over where they're drafted are subject to the inconsistencies of the laws in the state where the late-April sorting hat has sent them to reside.

item.title: Dan Campbell: I thought we'd get fourth-and-1, if not I knew we'd get the ball back
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Dan Campbell made the most Dan Campbell-like decision he could make on Sunday when the Lions faced fourth-and-1 at their own 24-yard line with the score tied and 4:53 remaining in the fourth quarter: He went for it.
item.content:encoded:
Dan Campbell made the most Dan Campbell-like decision he could make on Sunday when the Lions faced fourth-and-1 at their own 24-yard line with the score tied and 4:53 remaining in the fourth quarter: He went for it.

Campbell may be the only coach in the NFL who would have gone for it in that situation, and it didn't work, as Jahmyr Gibbs was tackled for a loss of two yards, putting the Packers in range for what would ordinarily be a chip-shot field goal to take the lead late in the fourth quarter.

But while the decision didn't work in the moment, it turned out OK for the Lions, who blocked the Packers' field goal attempt and then marched down the field for a game-winning field goal of their own as time expired. Campbell explained his thinking after the game.

"I thought we would get it, number one. I really believed we would get that. Number two, I knew we would get the ball back if it didn't work out. Those were the two thoughts," Campbell said.

That's solid reasoning. Only needing a yard with Gibbs and a good offensive line, it's easy to see why Campbell thought his team would get it.

But the second point is more important: Campbell wanted to ensure that the Lions would get the ball back with time to score. If the Lions had punted, there was the risk that the Packers would not only score on their subsequent possession, but run the remaining 4:53 off the clock and score with no time left. By giving the Packers the ball back deep in their own territory, Campbell at least knew the Packers wouldn't be able to mount a long drive that took all the remaining time off the clock.

Instead, after the Packers missed that field, it was the Lions who took over with 3:21 remaining and a long field ahead of them, and the Lions' long drive allowed them to run out the clock before kicking their game-winning field goal.

Campbell was wrong when he thought his team would make the fourth-and-1, but right that his team would get the ball back. And when his team got the ball back, it won the game.

item.title: Travis Kelce moves to No. 5 all-time in receptions, passes Marvin Harrison, Cris Carter
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Chiefs have been mostly stymied on offense throughout Sunday night’s matchup with the Seahawks.
item.content:encoded:
The Chiefs have been mostly stymied on offense throughout Sunday night’s matchup with the Seahawks.

But the unit did make some history in the fourth quarter of the contest.

Tight end Travis Kelce moved into No. 5 all time in receptions with 1,103, passing Marvin Harrison.

He had tied Harrison (1,102) and Cris Carter (1,101) earlier in the contest.

Kelce has a long way to go to the next player on the list, as Jason Witten is at No. 4 with 1,228 career catches. Jerry Rice is atop the list (1,549), followed by Larry Fitzgerald (1,432), and Tony Gonzalez (1,325).

With 13:11 in the fourth quarter, quarterback Patrick Mahomes found Kelce over the middle on third-and-6 to move the chains. Kelce ended up taking the historic catch 19 yards.

With the reception, Kelce now has three receptions for 41 yards so far on Sunday.

The Chiefs trail Seattle 13-3 midway through the fourth quarter.

item.title: Rashid Shaheed questionable to return to Seahawks-Chiefs with knee injury
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Seahawks have an injury concern with one of their key weapons.
item.content:encoded:
The Seahawks have an injury concern with one of their key weapons.

Seattle announced receiver/returner Rashid Shaheed is questionable to return with a knee injury.

Shaheed did not return the second-half kickoff, with Tory Horton performing those duties.

Shaheed had a 32-yard punt return during the first half.

UPDATE 10:35 p.m. ET: Shaheed has been downgraded to out. Additionally, running back Velus Jones Jr. is out with a hamstring injury.
